Rachel / Sara — tagging in legal perspective. Proposed contract language (short form) we can offer: 

"No Model Improvement Use: Redwood shall not access, use, or process Customer Data for the purpose of training, fine-tuning, evaluating for model improvement, or deriving model weights or optimizations for any model owned or operated by Redwood or its affiliates, other than as strictly necessary to provide the Services agreed herein. Any use beyond providing the Services requires Customer's prior written consent."

"Output Ownership: Customer retains all right, title, and interest in and to Customer Data and any Outputs generated solely from Customer Data. Redwood disclaims any ownership interest in Outputs and will not assert derivative rights or re-use Outputs for commercial model development."

Operational evidence we can attach:
- Ops runbook excerpt showing request routing, cache lifetimes, and log retention policies (ops-evidence-runbook.pdf).
- Subprocessor CSV (Redwood_Subprocessor_List_20260515.csv) with country columns and processing roles.
- A short attestation template we can sign confirming no training use.

Two caveats to flag for legal:
1) telemetry/usage metrics: we have limited monitoring telemetry (latency, error rates, aggregate token counts) that is not customer-content but may be processed for service integrity. We can exclude any customer-content telemetry from any learning pipelines.
2) forensic requests: exceptional security investigations might require temporary access by a specialist; we can contractually require notification and limits.

If Acme's redline includes retention thresholds or on-prem KMS requirements, please flag and we'll evaluate operational feasibility; we may need a Private deployment quote for stronger KMS/residency controls.
